newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia to increase share of iron ore/coal trades.
newsitem.headline: Asia to increase share of iron ore/coal trades.

text.p: Asia will increase its share of the iron ore and metallurgical coal trade over the next few years, mainly because of brisk demand in its growing economies, an analyst for BHP Transport Pty Ltd of Australia said on Thursday.

Michael Dunn, market analysis manager of BHP Transport, said at the 5th International Bulk Congress in Singapore that Asia will be buying 58 percent of the world's seaborne iron ore and metallurgical coal by 2002.
"Asian iron imports will grow to some 250 million tonnes in 2002, and if the implied growth is continued to 2010, they will be 300 million tonnes in that year," Dunn said.
Metallurgical coal imports, on the other hand, will reach 118 million tonnes in 2002 and rise to 130 million tonnes in 2010, he added.

"Capacity expansions will again require more metallurgical coal imports, particularly in India, where large increases in coal demand cannot be met by domestic production," Dunn said, alluding to plans by India to sharply expand steel output.
New blast furnaces are also being constructed in Asia and should come on stream in Taiwan, South Korea and China.
The new blast furnaces will allow Asian output of primary iron to rise to 280 million tonnes in 2002 and 325 million tonnes in 2010.
"Under this scenario, the Asian region will be producing half the world's primary iron by 2002 and will become the dominant producer after that," Dunn said.
BHP Transport is a unit of The Broken Hill Proprietary Company Ltd, Australia's biggest company.
